ajay.patel: quick FYI — bringup of llamaX-13B-q4 with our new quant kernels shows reproducible mismatch between KV-cache lookup and attention anchors past ~18k tokens :thinking_face:

sylvia: can you paste a tiny repro or logs? is this only on q4 or on fp16 too? :eyes:

ajay.patel: only seen on q4 so far. minimal repro attached below, run with --seq 20000 --stride 1024. output shows `kv_idx` suddenly jumps and we get token misalignment after the jump.

```
# simplified run CLI
python -m redwood.repro.longkv --model llamaX-13B-q4 --seq 20000 --batch 1
[INFO] kv_idx=18432 next_token="the"
[WARN] kv_idx mismatch: expected=18431 actual=18432
[DEBUG] attn_anchor[1023]=0.00012

# downstream: generation diverges at step 18435
```

leo: hmmm. could be a phase-to-index rounding when we quantize rotary angles. i've seen missed floor/ceil off-by-one after compressing float->int map. does the repro set `rope_scale` to 1.0?

ajay.patel: yes rope_scale=1.0. i tried forcing float computation path and the issue goes away (fp16 path fine). so likely quant path math. also repro on both CUDA and ROCm (weird).

maureen: can you run the diagnostic that dumps the rotary phase buffer and the computed index mapping for a couple tokens around the jump? something like `--dump-rotary 18428:18436`. will help check interpolation error vs kv indexing.

ajay.patel: running now, pushing logs to s3://redwood-test/kv-repro/1799019999/rotary-dump.log — posted snippet below:

```
# rotary dump excerpt (tokens 18430..18436)
token 18430 phase_raw=1.234567e+02 phase_q=123 phi_frac=0.99992 mapped_idx=18430
token 18431 phase_raw=1.234580e+02 phase_q=123 phi_frac=0.00003 mapped_idx=18432  <-- jump here
token 18432 phase_raw=1.234592e+02 phase_q=124 phi_frac=0.00045 mapped_idx=18433
```

leo: that phi_frac jump makes me think amplitude clamping is being applied inconsistently across kv and attn path after quantization. maybe one path uses rounding, the other truncation.

maureen: can you also run with `--kv-mode=legacy` vs `--kv-mode=packed`? if packed packs indices into uint16 we might be overflowing at that boundary.

ajay.patel: did both. packed shows exact same symptom. legacy slightly different offset but still a jump. reproduced on bench machine and CI runner.

ci-bot: test-run 1799019999-kv-repro (longseq) completed: 1 failed, 12 passed. failure: longkv/rotary-index-consistency. logs: https://ci.redwood.test/runs/1799019999

sylvia: thanks, great repro. assigning to eng-ml kernel owners. hypothesis: quant kernel uses int16 lut for ropescale with a rounding bias; need to align with attention path that computes effective index. if true, a small patch to the lut interpolation (use linear interpolation instead of nearest) should fix.

leo: i'll try a micro-patch to the quant kernel to switch to linear interp and add a unit test that sweeps sequences 16k..21k. will push draft PR and link.

ajay.patel: awesome. created ticket TICKET-ML-3421 and uploaded reproducer and raw dumps. leaving the thread here, ping me if you need extra logs. :thumbsup:
